title: Build every warehouse's pick list at once

blocks.text: The fulfilment service builds the morning pick lists with one task per warehouse, on a `ForkJoinPool` that the service creates at start-up and passes in. The morning run is called from a scheduler thread, not from the pool. With six warehouses it takes six times as long as one, although the pool has room for all six. Since two warehouses started sharing a cross-dock (each task waits until its partner's task has started), the run doesn't finish at all. And when one warehouse's data is broken, the alert should name that warehouse's own exception type, not a generic wrapper.
Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/PickLists.java`: `buildAll(...)` builds every warehouse's list and returns them in the order of the tasks.

When you're done, all the warehouse tasks run at the same time on the service's pool, partners finish, and a warehouse task that throws makes `buildAll` throw that exception's type. About four lines in total.

cases.says: every warehouse's list comes back, in the order of the tasks
no tasks give an empty list
two warehouse tasks that each wait for the other to start both finish, because they run at the same time
every task runs on the pool the service gave, even though the caller is not one of its threads
a warehouse task that throws makes the run throw that same exception type, not a wrapper

origin.section: A Failure Reaches the Caller Through invoke() or join(), and execute() Keeps It in the Task

concepts: fork() called from a thread that is no pool's worker schedules the task in the common pool, not in a pool you created.
invoke() waits for one task, so tasks handed over one invoke at a time never run together; submitting all before joining any runs them together.
invoke() and join() rethrow a task's unchecked exception as its own type, get() wraps it in an ExecutionException, and after execute() the exception stays in the task.
